definitions.explanation: A long, thin piece of wood or other material.
A straight line drawn on paper.

examples.english: I drew a line on the ground with a stick.

notes:
{棒|ぼう} is any straight, rigid length of material — a stick, pole, rod, or bar. Sense 2 extends this shape to marks on a surface: a straight stroke of the pen, or the bars of a bar chart.

The word is shape-based, not function-based, which is why it appears in so many compounds: whatever the object is for, if it is long and straight it can be a {棒|ぼう}.

Common compounds:
- ⟦{鉄棒|てつぼう}→てつぼう：17912_tetsubou⟧: the horizontal bar in gymnastics
- {棒|ぼう}⟦グラフ→グラフ：04864_gurafu⟧: bar graph
- ⟦{泥棒|どろぼう}→どろぼう：01688_dorobou⟧: thief (historically opaque — the modern word is not felt as containing 'stick')
- {棒読|ぼうよ}み: reading aloud in a flat monotone, as though the pitch were drawn with a ruler

Idioms:
- {棒|ぼう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{振|ふ}る→ふる：01983_furu⟧: to throw away or waste something you had built up — effort, money, a career.
- ⟦{犬|いぬ}→いぬ：00632_inu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{歩|ある}けば→あるく：00538_aruku⟧{棒|ぼう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{当|あ}たる→あたる：01860_ataru⟧: 'even a dog that walks about will bump into a stick.' A proverb used both ways — act and you may meet misfortune, or act and you may stumble on luck.

Similar words: a ⟦{杖|つえ}→杖：12862_tsue⟧ is a stick used for support when walking; a ⟦{竿|さお}→竿：24133_sao⟧ is a long slender pole, as for fishing or hanging laundry.
